string.description: The action to take when the policy matches: `ALLOW`, `BLOCK`, or `REJECT`.

Connection-state matching mode: `ALL` (any state), `RESPOND_ONLY` (established/related returns), or `CUSTOM` (match the states listed in `connection_states`). Optional: if omitted the controller assigns it (defaults to `ALL`) and the provider round-trips the value so updates are accepted.

list.description: Connection states matched when `connection_state_type` is `CUSTOM` (`NEW`, `ESTABLISHED`, `RELATED`, `INVALID`). Optional: leave unset for `ALL`/`RESPOND_ONLY` and the controller manages it; the provider round-trips the value so a `CUSTOM` policy's states are not dropped on update (which the firmware rejects with HTTP 400).

bool.description: When `true`, UniFi automatically creates a matching rule to allow established/related return traffic. Recommended for `ALLOW` policies. Defaults to `false`.

string.description: A description for the policy.

list.description: List of client MAC addresses to match. Used when `matching_target` is `CLIENT`.

string.description: ID of a `unifi_firewall_group` (address-group type) to match. Used when `matching_target` is `IP` with `matching_target_type = OBJECT`.

list.description: List of IP addresses or CIDR ranges to match. Used when `matching_target` is `IP`.

string.description: What to match: `ANY`, `NETWORK`, `CLIENT`, `IP`, `DEVICE`, `MAC`, or `WEB` (domains/FQDN).
How the matching target is specified (`ANY`, `SPECIFIC`, `LIST`, `OBJECT`). Managed by the UniFi controller; the provider round-trips it so updates are accepted.

list.description: List of UniFi network IDs to match. Used when `matching_target` is `NETWORK`.

string.description: Port(s) to match when `port_matching_type` is `SPECIFIC`. A single port (`161`) or a comma-separated list of ports/ranges (`80,443`, `8000-8100`). Leave unset for no port match.
ID of a `unifi_firewall_group` (port-group type) to match. Used when `port_matching_type` is `OBJECT`.
How to match ports: `ANY`, `SPECIFIC`, or `OBJECT` (port group).

list.description: List of domains/FQDNs to match. Used when `matching_target` is `WEB`.

string.description: The ID of the firewall zone this endpoint belongs to. Use the `unifi_firewall_zone` data source to look up zone IDs by name.

single_nested.description: The destination endpoint of the policy.

bool.description: Whether the policy is enabled. Defaults to `true`.

string.description: ICMP type matching mode. Managed by the UniFi controller; the provider round-trips it so updates are accepted.
ICMPv6 type matching mode. Managed by the UniFi controller; the provider round-trips it so updates are accepted.
The ID of the firewall policy.

int64.description: The ordering index of the policy within its zone-pair, assigned by the controller. **Read-only:** UniFi does not accept a client-supplied index on create or update (the policy is always appended to the end of its source/destination zone-pair), and the supported API exposes no reorder operation, so policy ordering cannot be managed through this provider. Reorder policies in the UniFi UI if needed.

string.description: The IP version to match: `BOTH`, `IPV4`, or `IPV6`. Defaults to `IPV4`.

bool.description: Whether to log packets matching this policy. Defaults to `false`.

string.description: The name of the firewall policy.

The protocol to match: `all`, `tcp`, `udp`, `tcp_udp`, `icmp`, or `icmpv6`. Defaults to `all`. Note: for `icmp`/`icmpv6` policies the controller rejects `create_allow_respond = true` (`FirewallPolicyCreateRespondTrafficPolicyNotAllowed`) — keep it `false` and add an explicit reverse policy if you need the reply.
The name of the site the firewall policy belongs to.

list.description: List of client MAC addresses to match. Used when `matching_target` is `CLIENT`.
